title: Region-aware fallback graph and automated deprecation workflow for pinned model versions
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem statement:
Customers can pin to a model version (e.g., gpt-ax.v1) for stability. Today, when a pinned model becomes unavailable in a region (out of capacity), is deprecated, or fails runtime checks, behavior is inconsistent: some requests error, some fall back to unrelated variants, and others silently switch to smaller models causing quality regressions. This causes production incidents, confused customers, and support load.

Goal:
Design and implement a deterministic, configurable fallback graph and an automated deprecation workflow for pinned versions. The system should: 1) prefer region-local compatible variants first, 2) respect customer pinning semantics (allow explicit opt-in to automatic downgrade), 3) surface deprecation notices and allow staged auto-migrations, and 4) integrate with published performance profiles so fallback choices minimize unit-cost and quality regressions.

Scope (this ticket):
- Define fallback graph ordering and policy primitives (region preference, variant affinity, quantization compatibility, and cost/latency thresholds).
- Add a new pinning policy schema (fallback_policy) to the model pin API and console.
- Implement runtime routing changes to evaluate fallback_policy at request routing time.
- Deprecation automation: signals, notification cadence, and optional auto-migration after X days.
- Publish changes to performance-profile docs so console/SDK can surface expected trade-offs for fallbacks.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- New pricing changes, per-tenant legal notice flows, and large-scale data migrations for already-pinned customers (those will be handled in follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Define fallback graph documentation with ordering rules (region -> model_variant -> quantization -> smaller-arch) published to the internal model onboarding spec.
Add fallback_policy to pinning API: documented fields and validation; schema published and accepted by SDK team.
Router uses fallback_policy to make deterministic routing decisions with telemetry showing correct decision path in 95% of tests.
Deprecation pipeline triggers warning emails + console banners at T-30, T-14, T-7 days; optional auto-migrate at T+7 days when customer opt-in enabled.
End-to-end integration test coverage for three failure scenarios: region OOS, model crash loop, performance-profile regression (latency > SLO).
No regression to existing pinning behavior for customers with fallback_policy set to 'strict' (zero automatic migration).
design_notes: High-level design: maintain a directed fallback graph per model family. Nodes represent model variants (same base architecture + compatible tokenizer), edges have tags: region_affinity, quantization_compatible, perf_delta_estimate. Router evaluates policy: 1) match exact pinned version in requested region, 2) region_local_variant with perf_delta < configured threshold, 3) cross-region read-replica if policy allows and latency budget permits, 4) quantized/optimized build of same version, 5) smaller model sibling with documented perf drop. Deprecation flow uses a three-phase lifecycle: notice -> scheduled deprecate -> enforcement (if auto-migrate enabled). Performance-profile publishing must include perf_delta_estimate metadata to allow automated cost/quality tradeoff selection.
implementation_plan: API: extend POST /pins and PATCH /pins/{id} to accept fallback_policy object (fields: mode [strict|permissive|opt-in], max_perf_regression_pct, allow_cross_region, auto_migrate_days, notification_emails).
Console: UI for pin details to show current fallback_policy, preview of fallback graph and perf deltas; toggle for auto-migrate opt-in.
Runtime: router change: implement DecisionEngine component that evaluates fallback graph nodes in priority order and records decision path in tracing headers.
Telemetry: add fallback_decision event (reason, chosen_node, perf_estimate, latency_budget_hit) to observability pipeline.
Deprecation service: cron job that aggregates deprecation signals and drives notices; integrates with support-runbook generator.
Docs: model onboarding guide updated with fallback best practices and required perf-profile metadata fields.
testing_plan: Unit tests for DecisionEngine path selection, synthetic traffic tests simulating (1) regional capacity loss, (2) model runtime crash loop, (3) SLO breach. Canary rollout to a small internal tenant using permissive policy, collect telemetry for one week, then expand. Create regression tests for strict-mode pinned customers ensuring no auto-migration occurs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal alpha (console + API + router flags) with one internal tenant and two models. Phase 2: opt-in beta for customers (opt-in via console toggle). Phase 3: GA where fallback_policy is available to all customers; strict remains default for previously-pinned customers to avoid surprise migrations. Scheduled full rollout target: two internal cycles after QA signoff.
